item.title: 2026 Functional Exercise Activity Design: Bridging Movement Science and Practice
item.description:
As an Adjunct Lecturer in the Department of Leisure and Recreation Management at Taipei City University of Science and Technology, I focus on transforming a passion for fitness into a scientifically grounded career. My teaching methodology bridges the gap between movement science and real-world functional application.

Foundational Movement, Functional Equipment, Activity Design!

2026 Functional Exercise Activity Design

Bridging the Gap Between Science and Application

In my course, 2026 Functional Exercise Activity Design, I guide students through the principles of functional movement, drawing inspiration from high-performance protocols like HYROX and the NSCA’s Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning. By integrating English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) methodologies and active learning strategies like Think-Pair-Share and scaffolding, my approach ensures that future professionals don’t just memorize terms but deeply understand the biomechanics of multi-planar movement.

This instructional framework prepares students for advanced practice and coaching certifications, focusing on movement efficiency, velocity-based training, and the practical application of functional strength equipment.

Watch Course Description on YouTube

Core Pillars of My Instruction

The curriculum is built around three critical domains:

  1. Foundational Movement Science: We explore kinetic chains, bioenergetics, and biomechanics. It’s not just about naming muscles; it’s about understanding how the human body generates power across the sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes during dynamic, real-world activities.
  2. Applied Functional Technique: From kettlebell swings and free weights to velocity-based training and cardiovascular intervals, students utilize a wide array of functional implements to refine their coaching and demonstration skills.
  3. Activity Design & Programming: This is where science becomes art. Students learn to design safe, effective functional programs for diverse goals—from strength-endurance to high-intensity functional training—and for populations ranging from athletic competitors to those seeking improved daily mobility.

Inside the Classroom: Practical Teaching Demonstrations

Translating Movement Science to Client Success

A proficient strength and conditioning coach must be able to analyze a client’s foundational movement patterns—such as the hinge, squat, push, pull, and carry—instantly. In this segment, I explain how to assess movement efficiency using functional tools like free weights. By deeply understanding kinetic linking, future instructors can provide precise verbal cues and drastically reduce the risk of client injury.

Watch on YouTube

Mastering the Functional Assessment and Framework

Success in functional training relies on identifying movement limitations and properly introducing equipment. This video captures how I teach students to conduct dynamic movement assessments and establish the foundational framework for safely integrating kettlebells and velocity-based metrics into a client’s routine.

Watch on YouTube

Long-Term Programming Strategy: Manipulating Variables for Functional Fitness

To prevent client plateaus and overtraining, professionals must master the art of periodization for functional fitness. Here, I illustrate how to strategically manipulate FITT-VP variables specifically for functional and HYROX-style conditioning, ensuring sustainable, long-term adaptations.

Watch on YouTube

The Golden Rules of Functional Adaptation

Generic workouts fail to produce movement proficiency. In this lecture highlight, I break down the core principles of functional training: Specificity, Overload, and Movement Quality. I place a strong emphasis on aligning energy systems and functional mechanics with a client’s unique health or performance goals.

Watch on YouTube

Professional Excellence & Certification

The ultimate goal of this methodology is to ensure students are ready to lead clients toward their functional goals with absolute confidence and scientific backing.

  • Instructional Focus: Meticulously aligned with NSCA-CSCS domains and advanced functional training standards.
  • Pedagogical Innovation: Integration of EMI active learning strategies and hands-on application with functional strength equipment.
  • Industry Expertise: Grounded in my experience as a PhD candidate and holder of NSCA-CSCS*D, ACSM-CEP, and ACSM-EP certifications.
